Problem 524. Reading a layered map legend (B2)
Knowledge context.
A map legend translates symbols into properties. One location may have several properties at the same time.
Given facts.

Legend: tree=forest, wavy line=river, double line=road, arch=bridge, square=village, triangle=hill. Cells: A1 has forest, hill, road; A2 has bridge, river; B1 has forest, river, road; B2 has road, village. Cross-domain check: on a field sketch, 1 cm represents 6 km and two checkpoints are 8 cm apart.
Rules.

A cell satisfies the task only if it has every required attribute. Extra attributes do not disqualify it unless the task says so. For the cross-domain check, real distance = sketch distance × kilometres per centimetre.
Task.
Which cell or cells satisfy all of these conditions: hill, road? Explain by intersecting the clues. Cross-domain check: what real distance separates the checkpoints?
Step-by-step solution.
1. Convert the requested symbols into the attribute set ['hill', 'road']. 2. Check each cell for every required attribute. 3. The matching set is ['A1']. Cross-domain check: 8×6=48 km.
Answer.
A1 Cross-domain answer: 48 km.
Knowledge takeaway.
Map reading often means intersecting clues rather than recognizing one symbol in isolation.
Formal model.
Set model; each cell has an attribute set; return cells whose set is a superset of the required set.

G6. Choosing a settlement site
Problem 526. Choosing a safe settlement site: case 1
Knowledge context.
Human settlements depend on several factors at once. Some conditions may be compulsory while others are preferences.
Given facts.

Candidate sites: Site A: water=yes, road=yes, flood-zone=no, nearby farmland score=2; Site B: water=yes, road=no, flood-zone=no, nearby farmland score=4; Site C: water=yes, road=yes, flood-zone=yes, nearby farmland score=4; Site D: water=no, road=yes, flood-zone=no, nearby farmland score=6. Cross-domain check: a local committee has 12 members, requires at least 7 present for quorum, and 11 are present.
Rules.

A valid site must have water, road access, and must not be in the flood zone. Among valid sites, choose the one with the highest farmland score. For the cross-domain check, quorum exists when present members ≥ the stated threshold.
Task.
Which site should be selected under the stated mandatory conditions and preference rule? Cross-domain check: is quorum met?
Step-by-step solution.

1. Separate mandatory conditions from the preference. 2. Filtering by water, road, and flood safety leaves ['Site A']. 3. Compare only the farmland scores of feasible sites: Site A=2. 4. Site A has the best score among valid sites. Cross-domain check: compare 11 with 7; 11≥7 is true.
Answer.
Site A. Cross-domain answer: quorum is met.
Knowledge takeaway.
Good decisions first satisfy hard constraints and only then optimize among the remaining options.
Formal model.
Constraint-satisfaction problem followed by a score maximization over feasible options.
